title: Duke as pianist and arranger, and the Carnegie Hall rush
summary: Tizol says Duke could not play a written piano part but wrote perfectly for his men, writing for days for the Carnegie Hall concert and writing Spanish-flavoured parts for Juan.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: You know, that's why the whole trouble with a lot of people -- you couldn't give Duke a piano part and say, 'Play this piano part; he was not that type of piano player. He couldn't play it. He played his own stuff, because there was no part to it. But Duke Ellington wasn't a man where somebody could give him a piano part and say play that -- no, he couldn't do that.
No, I don't think so, no. He plays

he learn the melody, and after the melody, he goes for himself, you know? But still, he was a hell of an arranger, but nobody could figure out how he did it. But he was good, because he did it for Ziegfeld Follies, for the first concert at Carnegie Hall. We stayed there in his house, writing so much until one time he sent for Doctor -- what was his name, his doctor?
No, no. Dr. -- the fellow that jumped in the pier.
Dr. Logan. He gave us some shots, you know, for the eyes from working so hard. He was writing them for ... A couple of days and nights without any sleep.

He was writing for awhile for that concert at Carnegie Hall, and a lot of people thought that he didn't know what he was doing, but Duke Ellington formed his band -- maybe he could not arrange for Jimmy Lunceford's band or this and the other, but he knew how to write for Duke Ellington's boys, because he was writing for the boys, for the instrument.
The way that man sounded on that instrument.
Yeah, he played, for instance -- a C-note he knew what I could do better than I could on my trombone. He would write that

Spanish music, and let me play Spanish music and so forth, or something to and use me with his saxophone player -- like a chorus, four saxaphones and one trombone. A lot of tunes for me playing the melody, behind the other saxaphone.
Oh, he really knew what he was doing, but a lot of people thought he couldn't do it, but he was not doing it. that.
